steps.title: Three stories, one window
paragraphs: At lunchtime, a football smashed through the school kitchen window.
Ayo, who kicked it, says it was an accident and the wind did it. Ms Rivera, the cook, says she nearly lost a whole tray of jelly. Jun, the goalkeeper, says it was the best save he never made.
Same event, three stories. Who tells it changes everything.

cards.title: Perspective
cards.body: Every character notices different things, cares about different things and feels differently about what happens. When you retell an event from a new point of view, the events stay the same, but what the narrator notices, thinks and feels changes.

cards.title: The picnic, three ways
cards.prompt: One stolen sandwich, three narrators. What does each one notice?

versions.text: The sandwich was right there, glowing like treasure. I waited until Dad looked away. Then I struck. Best. Day. Ever.
versions.knows: Only what Biscuit the dog notices and wants: the sandwich. He has no idea Dad is upset.

versions.text: Dad turned for one second to find the ketchup. When he turned back, his sandwich was gone, and Biscuit was licking his lips. Dad sighed. Why had he ever thought a picnic was a good idea?
versions.knows: Only Dad's thoughts. He can guess what Biscuit did, but not what Biscuit was thinking.

versions.text: Dad turned to find the ketchup, and Biscuit saw his chance. While the dog gulped down the sandwich, delighted, Dad wondered why he had ever planned a picnic, and little Mia, who had seen everything, decided to keep the secret.
versions.knows: Everything: what Biscuit wants, what Dad wonders, and what Mia decides.

cards.title: Keep it steady
cards.body: Once you choose a point of view, stick with it. A first-person narrator can't suddenly know another character's thoughts, and a third-person story shouldn't slip into I. If you want a new view, start a new part or chapter.

cards.title: Same picnic, different views
cards.prompt: Tap the two words that show how differently Biscuit and Dad see the same picnic.
cards.text: Biscuit thought the picnic was the greatest day of his life. Dad thought it was a disaster.

prompts: Which version was the most fun to write, and why?
What did one narrator notice that the others didn't?
